title: CELPIP Scores: CLB Levels & Express Entry Points
summary: How CELPIP's 1–12 levels map to the CLB, why CLB 7 and CLB 9 are the numbers to know, and how each skill counts.

nodes.label: = CLB level
nodes.note: CELPIP level maps directly to CLB

chunks.heading: One level per skill, mapped to the CLB
chunks.body: CELPIP reports a **level from 1 to 12 for each skill** (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking), and each level **corresponds directly to a Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) level**. There's no single 'overall' number — immigration looks at your **per-skill CLB**.
chunks.realExample: A report of Listening 9, Reading 8, Writing 9, Speaking 9 means CLB 9/8/9/9 — and Express Entry scores each skill, so your lowest skill can hold back your points.
chunks.memoryHook: A level per skill = a CLB per skill. No overall — your weakest skill matters.

chunks.heading: CLB 7 and CLB 9 are the magic numbers
chunks.body: For Express Entry, **CLB 7 in all four skills** is a common minimum (e.g. for Federal Skilled Worker eligibility), and **CLB 9 in all four** unlocks the **maximum language points** in the CRS. Pushing every skill to 9 can be worth a large jump in your ranking score.
chunks.realExample: Moving from CLB 8 to CLB 9 across all skills can add substantial CRS points — often more than any other single improvement — so it's a high-value target if you're close.
chunks.memoryHook: CLB 7 = common minimum. CLB 9 = maximum points. Aim every skill at 9 if you can.

chunks.heading: Your lowest skill is the constraint
chunks.body: Because Express Entry awards points **per skill**, your **weakest skill caps your language points**. So identify your lowest CELPIP level and focus practice there — lifting the weakest skill usually adds more points than improving one you're already strong in.
chunks.realExample: If you're CLB 9 in three skills but CLB 7 in Writing, your Writing is the one dragging your points — targeted Writing practice is the fastest CRS gain.
chunks.memoryHook: Points are per skill. Fix the weakest link — that's where the points are.

chunks.heading: Fast results, valid two years, no penalty
chunks.body: CELPIP results arrive in a **few business days** and are **valid for two years**. Multiple-choice sections have **no wrong-answer penalty**, so always answer everything, and you can **retake** if a skill falls short of your target CLB.
chunks.realExample: A skill one level below target? Retake with focused practice on that skill — with fast results, you can slot a new report into your Express Entry profile quickly.
chunks.memoryHook: Results in days, valid 2 years, retakes allowed. No penalty — never leave blanks.

recall.a: As a level from 1 to 12 for each skill, with each level mapping directly to a Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) level — there's no single overall number.

recall.q: Why do CLB 7 and CLB 9 matter for Express Entry?
recall.a: CLB 7 in all skills is a common minimum, and CLB 9 in all skills unlocks the maximum language points in the CRS.

recall.q: Why does your weakest skill matter most?
recall.a: Express Entry awards points per skill, so your lowest CELPIP level caps your language points.

recall.q: Which skill should you focus practice on?
recall.a: Your lowest-scoring skill — lifting the weakest one usually adds the most CRS points.

recall.q: How quickly do CELPIP results come and how long are they valid?
recall.a: Results in a few business days, valid for two years.
